description: Abstract Training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with standard backpropagation through time (BPTT) can be challenging, especially in the presence of long input sequences. A practical alternative to reduce computational and memory overhead is to perform BPTT repeatedly over shorter segments of the training data set, corresponding to truncated BPTT.

title: Traceable, Enforceable, and Compensable Participation: A Participation Ledger for People-Centered AI Governance
creator: Rashid Mushkani
description: Abstract Participatory approaches are widely invoked in AI governance, yet participation rarely translates into durable influence. In public sector and civic AI systems, community contributions such as deliberations, annotations, prompts, and incident reports are typically recorded informally, weakly linked to system updates, and disconnected from enforceable rights or sustained compensation. As a result, participation is often symbolic rather than accountable.

title: Discrete Quantitative Isocapacitary Inequality: Fluctuation Estimates
creator: M. Cicalese, L. Kreutz, I. Mansoor
description: Abstract . The classical isocapacitary inequality states that, among all sets of fixed volume, the ball uniquely minimizes the capacity. While this result holds in the continuum, it fails in the discrete setting, where the isocapacitary problem may admit multiple minimizers.

title: HD 164604 c: a second giant planet on a 15-yr orbit and the constraint of the planet-planet mutual inclination This paper includes data gathered with the 6.5 meter Magellan Telescopes located at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. Facilities: MIKE, PFS, Hipparcos, Gaia astropy ( 8 ; 6 ; 7 ) , scipy ( 8
creator: Guang-Yao Xiao (肖光耀), Fabo Feng (冯发波), R. Paul Butler, Johanna K. Teske, Stephen A. Shectman, Jeffrey D. Crane, Sharon X. Wang (王雪凇)

title: Dirac mode localization in QCD near the crossover temperature
creator: Matteo Giordano, Tamás G. Kovács, Ferenc Pittler
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Matteo Giordano, Tamás G. Kovács, Ferenc Pittler. We study the localization properties of the low-lying Dirac eigenmodes in QCD near the crossover temperature, using staggered fermions on the lattice. We find that localized low modes, absent at low temperature, appear at a temperature T loc T_{\mathrm{loc}} in the range 155 ​ MeV ≤ T loc ≤ 158 ​ MeV 155\,\mathrm{MeV}\leq T_{\mathrm{loc}}\leq 158\,\mathrm{MeV} , in excellent agreement with the pseudocritical crossover temperature as determined from the chiral condensate and from the light-quark susceptibility.

title: Non-centred Bayesian inference for discrete-valued state-transition models: the Rippler algorithm
creator: James Neill, Lloyd A. C. Chapman, Chris Jewell
description: Abstract Stochastic state-transition models of infectious disease transmission can be used to deduce relevant drivers of transmission when fitted to data using statistically principled methods. Fitting this individual-level data requires inference on individuals’ unobserved disease statuses over time, which form a high-dimensional and highly correlated state space.

title: Linear Operators on Polynomials and K K -Positivity Preserver
creator: Philipp J. di Dio
description: Abstract A journey from analysis to algebra and back \frontmatter \preface These are the extended lecture notes of my lecture about Linear Operators on Polynomials, K -Positivity Preserver, and their Generators. The lecture was given at the University of Konstanz in the winter semester 2025/26.

title: Two-Scale Analysis of the Electrostatics of Dielectric Crystals: Emergence of Polarization Density and Boundary Charges Preprint: SIAM Multiscale Modeling and Simulation 24(1):162-186, 2026 (DOI: 10.1137/25M1747907)
creator: Shoham Sen, Yang Wang, Timothy Breitzman, Kaushik Dayal
description: Abstract Ionic crystals, such as solid electrolytes and complex oxides, are central to modern technologies for energy storage, sensing, actuation, and other functional applications. An important fundamental issue in the atomic and quantum-scale modeling of these materials is defining the macroscopic polarization.

title: CMAD: Cooperative Multi-Agent Diffusion via Stochastic Optimal Control
creator: Riccardo Barbano, Alexander Denker & Željko Kereta, Runchang Li, Francisco Vargas
description: Abstract Continuous-time generative models have achieved remarkable success in image restoration and synthesis. However, controlling the composition of multiple pre-trained models remains an open challenge. Current approaches largely treat composition as an algebraic composition of probability densities, such as via products or mixtures of experts. This perspective assumes the target distribution is known explicitly, which is almost never the case.

title: Multi-Environment MDPs with Prior and Universal Semantics
creator: Benjamin Bordais, Jean-François Raskin, Université Libre de Bruxelles
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Bordais, Jean-François Raskin, Université Libre de Bruxelles. Multiple-environment Markov decision processes (MEMDPs) equip an MDP with several probabilistic transition functions (one per possible environment) so that the state is observable but the environment is not. Previous work studies two semantics: (i) the universal semantics, where an adversary picks the environment; and (ii) the prior semantics, where the environment is drawn once before execution from a fixed distribution. We clarify the relation between these semantics.

title: Towards Learning a Generalizable 3D Scene Representation from 2D Observations
creator: Martin Gromniak 1,2, Jan-Gerrit Habekost 1, Sebastian Kamp 1, Sven Magg 3 and Stefan Wermter 1 1 - University of Hamburg - Department of Informatics, Hamburg - Germany 2 - ZAL Center of Applied Aeronautical Research, Hamburg - Germany 3 - Hamburger Informatik Technologie-Center e.V. (HITeC), Hamburg
description: Abstract We introduce a Generalizable Neural Radiance Field approach for predicting 3D workspace occupancy from egocentric robot observations. Unlike prior methods operating in camera-centric coordinates, our model constructs occupancy representations in a global workspace frame, making it directly applicable to robotic manipulation. The model integrates flexible source views and generalizes to unseen object arrangements without scene-specific finetuning.

title: Parameterized Complexity of Finding a Maximum Common Vertex Subgraph Without Isolated Vertices
creator: Palash Dey, Anubhav Dhar, Ashlesha Hota, Sudeshna Kolay, Aritra Mitra
description: Abstract In this paper, we study the Maximum Common Vertex Subgraph problem: Given two input graphs G 1 , G 2 G_{1},G_{2} and a non-negative integer h h , is there a common subgraph H H on at least h h vertices such that there is no isolated vertex in H H .

title: Optimal Initialization in Depth: Lyapunov Initialization and Limit Theorems for Deep Leaky ReLU Networks
creator: Constantin Kogler, Tassilo Schwarz, Samuel Kittle
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Constantin Kogler, Tassilo Schwarz, Samuel Kittle. The development of effective initialization methods requires an understanding of random neural networks. In this work, a rigorous probabilistic analysis of deep unbiased Leaky ReLU networks is provided. We prove a Law of Large Numbers and a Central Limit Theorem for the logarithm of the norm of network activations, establishing that, as the number of layers increases, their growth is governed by a parameter called the Lyapunov exponent.

title: Improving Quantum Multi-Objective Optimization with Archiving and Substitution
creator: Linus Ekstrøm, Takafumi Hosogi, Xavier Bonet-Monroig, Hao Wang, Thomas Bäck, Sebastian Schmitt
description: Abstract Finding optimal solutions of conflicting objectives is a daily matter in many industrial applications, with multi-objective optimization trying to find the best solutions to them. The advent of quantum computing has led to researchers wondering if the promised exponential advantage can be obtained for these problems by variational quantum multi-objective optimization (QMOO) algorithm.

title: Prior Smoothing for Multivariate Disease Mapping Models
creator: Garazi Retegui, María Dolores Ugarte, Jaione Etxeberria, Alan E. Gelfand
description: Abstract To date, we have seen the emergence of a large literature on multivariate disease mapping. That is, incidence of (or mortality from) multiple diseases is recorded at the scale of areal units where incidence (mortality) across the diseases is expected to manifest dependence.

title: Fluctuation-Response Design Rules for Nonequilibrium Flows
creator: Ying-Jen Yang, Ken A. Dill
description: Abstract Biological machines like molecular motors and enzymes operate in dynamic cycles representable as stochastic flows on networks. Current stochastic dynamics describes such flows on fixed networks. Here, we develop a scalable approach to network design in which local transition rates can be systematically varied to achieve global dynamical objectives.

title: Rotary Positional Embeddings as Phase Modulation: Theoretical Bounds on the RoPE Base for Long-Context Transformers
creator: Feilong Liu
description: Abstract Rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) are widely used in large language models to encode token positions through multiplicative rotations, yet their behavior at long context lengths remains poorly characterized. In this work, we reinterpret RoPE as phase modulation applied to a bank of complex oscillators, enabling analysis through classical signal processing theory.

title: Integrating granular data into a multilayer network: an interbank model of the euro area for systemic risk assessment The views expressed in this paper are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Central Bank.
creator: Ilias Aarab, Thomas Gottron, Andrea Colombo, Jörg Reddig, Annalaura Ianiro
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ilias Aarab, Thomas Gottron, Andrea Colombo, Jörg Reddig, Annalaura Ianiro. Micro-structural models of contagion and systemic risk emphasize that shock propagation is inherently multi-channel, spanning counterparty exposures, short-term funding and roll-over risk, securities cross-holdings, and common-asset (fire-sale) spillovers. Empirical implementations, however, often rely on stylized or simulated networks, or focus on a single exposure dimension, reflecting the practical difficulty of reconciling heterogeneous granular collections into a coherent representation with consistent identifiers and consolidation rules.

title: A generalization of Frenkel’s formula
creator: Shmuel Friedland
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Shmuel Friedland. We generalize Frenkel’s integral formula for traces of operators to operators. The resulting formula holds for bounded self-adjoint positive operators and p p -Schatten class of compact positive operators. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 81P47,94A40 1. Introduction Denote: \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}\supset\mathrm{H}_{n}\supset\mathrm{H}_{n,+}\supset\mathrm{H}_{n,++} the complex space of n\times n matrices, the real space of n\times n Hermitian matrices, the cone of positive semidefinite matrices, and the open set of positive definite matrices.

title: Lie Group Variational Integrator for the Geometrically Exact Rod with Circular Cross-Section Incorporating Cross-Sectional Deformation Journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
creator: Srishti Siddharth, Vivek Natarajan, Ravi N. Banavar
description: Abstract In this paper, we derive the continuous space-time equations of motion of a three-dimensional geometrically exact rod, or the Cosserat rod, incorporating planar cross-sectional deformation. We then adopt the Lie group variational integrator technique to obtain a discrete model of the rod incorporating both rotational motion and cross-sectional deformation as well.

title: Can LLMs Cook Jamaican Couscous? A Study of Cultural Novelty in Recipe Generation
creator: Florian Carichon, Romain Rampa, Golnoosh Farnadi
description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate and shape cultural content, ranging from narrative writing to artistic production. While these models demonstrate impressive fluency and generative capacity, prior work has shown that they also exhibit systematic cultural biases, raising concerns about stereotyping, homogenization, and the erasure of culturally specific forms of expression.

title: Weighting-Based Identification and Estimation in Graphical Models of Missing Data
creator: Anna Guo and Razieh Nabi Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Emory University
description: Abstract We propose a constructive algorithm for identifying complete data distributions in graphical models of missing data. The complete data distribution is unrestricted, while the missingness mechanism is assumed to factorize according to a conditional directed acyclic graph. Our approach follows an interventionist perspective in which missingness indicators are treated as variables that can be intervened on.

title: Note on the trace of random walks on pseudorandom graphs Thanks: Yiting Wang is supported by the European Research Council (ERC), via grant agreements “RANDSTRUCT” No. 101076777.
creator: Yaobin Chen, Yiting Wang
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yaobin Chen, Yiting Wang. We study the graph-theoretic properties of the trace of random walks on pseudorandom graphs. We show that for any ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 , there exists a constant C C such that the cover time of an ( n , d , λ ) (n,d,\lambda) -graph G G with d / λ ≥ C d/\lambda\geq C is at most ( 1 + ε ) ​ n ​ log ⁡ n (1+\varepsilon)n\log n , meaning the expected number of steps needed

title: A Jointly Efficient and Optimal Algorithm for Heteroskedastic Generalized Linear Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions Equal contributions
creator: Sanghwa Kim, Junghyun Lee, Se-Young Yun
description: Abstract We consider the problem of heteroskedastic generalized linear bandits (GLBs) with adversarial corruptions, which subsumes various stochastic contextual bandit settings, including heteroskedastic linear bandits and logistic/Poisson bandits. We propose HCW-GLB-OMD , which consists of two components: an online mirror descent (OMD)-based estimator and Hessian-based confidence weights to achieve corruption robustness.

title: Deriving and Validating Requirements Engineering Principles for Large-Scale Agile Development: An Industrial Longitudinal Study Conference: ; April, 2026; BRAZIL ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Software and its engineering Requirements analysis CCS: Software and its engineering Agile software d
creator: Hina Saeeda, Mijin Kim, Eric Knauss, Jesper Thyssen, Jesper Ørting, Jesper Lysemose Korsgaard, Niels Jørgen Strøm
description: Abstract . In large-scale agile systems development, the lack of a unified requirements engineering (RE) process is a major challenge, exacerbated by the absence of high-level guiding principles for effective requirements management. To address this challenge, we conducted a five-year longitudinal case study with Grundfos AB , in collaboration with the Software Centre in Sweden.

title: Three-loop QCD+QED corrections to on-shell quark renormalization Preprint: CPTNP-2026-005, ZU-TH 05/26
creator: Long Chen, Hong-Yang Han, Zhe Li, Marco Niggetiedt
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Long Chen, Hong-Yang Han, Zhe Li, Marco Niggetiedt. We present the three-loop QCD+QED mixed corrections to the on-shell quark mass and wave-function renormalization constants through orders 𝒪 ⁡ ( α s m ​ α n ) \mathcal{O}(\alpha_{s}^{m}\alpha^{n}) with m + n = 3 m+n=3 . We further derive the three-loop relation between the pole mass and the MS ¯ \overline{\text{MS}} mass of a heavy quark, including the complete mixed QCD+QED contributions.

title: RADAR: Benchmarking Vision-Language-Action Generalization via Real-World Dynamics, Spatial-Physical Intelligence, and Autonomous Evaluation Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; ; ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Computing methodologies
creator: Yuhao Chen 1,* , Zhihao Zhan 1,* , Xiaoxin Lin 1 , Zijian Song 1 , Hao Liu 1 , Qinhan Lyu 1 , Yubo Zu 1 , Xiao Chen 1 , Zhiyuan Liu 1 , Tao Pu 1,3 , Tianshui Chen 3,4 , Keze Wang 1,2,3 , Liang Lin 1,2,3 , Guangrun Wang 1,2,3,† Email: {chenyh387, zhanzhh6} (at) mail2.sysu.edu.cn, wanggrun (at) gmail.
description: Abstract . Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models have achieved remarkable progress in embodied intelligence; however, their evaluation remains largely confined to simulations or highly constrained real-world settings. This mismatch creates a substantial reality gap , where strong benchmark performance often masks poor generalization in diverse physical environments.

title: Sample Efficient Generative Molecular Optimization with Joint Self-Improvement
creator: Serra Korkmaz, Adam Izdebski, Jonathan Pirnay, Rasmus Møller-Larsen, Michal Kmicikiewicz, Pankhil Gawade, Dominik G. Grimm, Ewa Szczurek
description: Abstract Generative molecular optimization aims to design molecules with properties surpassing those of existing compounds. However, such candidates are rare and expensive to evaluate, yielding sample efficiency essential. Additionally, surrogate models introduced to predict molecule evaluations, suffer from distribution shift as optimization drives candidates increasingly out-of-distribution.

title: Cutoff Sobolev inequalities for local and non-local p p -energies on metric measure spaces
creator: Meng Yang
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Meng Yang. For p > 1 p>1 , we study subordination phenomena for local and non-local regular p p -energies on metric measure spaces. Under suitable geometric assumptions, we show that if a local regular p p -energy satisfies a Poincaré inequality together with a cutoff Sobolev inequality with scaling function Ψ \Psi , then all associated stable-like non-local p p -energies with scaling functions strictly below Ψ \Psi are regular and satisfy the corresponding non-local cutoff Sobolev inequalities.

title: A Human-Centric Framework for Data Attribution in Large Language Models DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Social and professional topics Intellectual property CCS: Computing methodologies Natural language generation CCS: Social and professional topics Socio-technical systems
creator: Amelie Wührl, Mattes Ruckdeschel, Kyle Lo, Anna Rogers
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Amelie Wührl, Mattes Ruckdeschel, Kyle Lo, Anna Rogers. In the current Large Language Model (LLM) ecosystem, creators have little agency over how their data is used, and LLM users may find themselves unknowingly plagiarizing existing sources. Attribution of LLM-generated text to LLM input data could help with these challenges, but so far we have more questions than answers: what elements of LLM outputs require attribution, what goals should it serve, how should it be implemented?

title: Fine-Tuning GPT-5 for GPU Kernel Generation
creator: Ali Tehrani, Yahya Emara, Essam Wissam, Wojciech Paluch, Waleed Atallah, Łukasz Dudziak, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ali Tehrani, Yahya Emara, Essam Wissam, Wojciech Paluch, Waleed Atallah, Łukasz Dudziak, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah. Developing efficient GPU kernels is essential for scaling modern AI systems, yet it remains a complex task due to intricate hardware architectures and the need for specialized optimization expertise.

title: Eliminating Delocalization Error through Localized Orbital Scaling Correction with Orbital Relaxation from Linear Response
creator: Yichen Fan, Jincheng Yu, Jiayi Du, Weitao Yang
description: Abstract Despite the great success Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) has achieved, the delocalization error remains a major challenge for commonly used density functional approximations (DFAs), resulting in systematic errors in ionization energies, electron affinities, band structures, and charge distributions.

title: Enhancing Predictability of Multi-Tenant DNN Inference for Autonomous Vehicles’ Perception
creator: Liangkai Liu 1 , Kang G. Shin 1 , Jinkyu Lee 2 , Chengmo Yang 3 , and Weisong Shi 3
description: Abstract Autonomous vehicles (AVs) rely on sensors and deep neural networks (DNNs) to perceive their surrounding environment and make maneuver decisions in real time. However, achieving real-time DNN inference in the AV’s perception pipeline is challenging due to the large gap between the computation requirement and the AV’s limited resources.

title: LaSSM: Efficient Semantic-Spatial Query Decoding via Local Aggregation and State Space Models for 3D Instance Segmentation
creator: Lei Yao, Yi Wang, Yawen Cui, Moyun Liu, and Lap-Pui Chau
description: Abstract Query-based 3D scene instance segmentation from point clouds has attained notable performance. However, existing methods suffer from the query initialization dilemma due to the sparse nature of point clouds and rely on computationally intensive attention mechanisms in query decoders. We accordingly introduce LaSSM , prioritizing simplicity and efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

title: Relative Chaos for C 0 C_{0} -Semigroups Beyond Topological Notions
creator: El-Mehdi Nafia, Aziz El Ghazouani, M’hamed El Omari
description: Abstract We investigate instability phenomena for linear evolution equations within the framework of C 0 C_{0} –semigroups on infinite–dimensional spaces. We show that Devaney chaos, being formulated in purely topological terms, may depend on the choice of topology and therefore fail to capture intrinsic dynamical behavior.

title: On the hyperreal dual Steenrod algebra
creator: Michael A. Hill, Michael J. Hopkins
description: Abstract . We compute the dual Steenrod algebra for Bredon homology with constant coefficients ℤ ¯ \underline{\mathbb{Z}} and ℤ ¯ / 2 \underline{\mathbb{Z}}/2 in the category of modules over M ​ U ( ( G ) ) MU^{((G))} , the norm to G = C 2 n G=C_{2^{n}} of M ​ U ℝ MU_{\mathbb{R}} .

title: Rational Points in Hyperbolic Regions and Multiplicative Diophantine Approximation on Manifolds
creator: Sam Chow, Rajula Srivastava, Niclas Technau, Han Yu
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Sam Chow, Rajula Srivastava, Niclas Technau, Han Yu. We establish the convergence theory of multiplicative Diophantine approximation for all non-degenerate, smooth manifolds. We also settle said convergence theory for all affine subspaces satisfying a highly generic and essentially optimal Diophantine condition. This answers a question of Beresnevich and Velani from 2005, while simultaneously sharpening results of Kleinbock and Margulis on the strong extremality of non-degenerate manifolds, and of Kleinbock on the strong extremality of affine subspaces.

title: Initial Guesses for Multicomponent Mean-Field Methods: Assessment and New Developments
creator: Denis G. Artiukhin
description: Abstract The convergence of self-consistent field equations in mean-field nuclear–electronic orbital methods strongly depends on the choice of initial guesses for quantum nuclei. Although several such guesses have been proposed in the literature, a systematic comparison of their performance as well as attempts of constructing novel approximations based on model tasks of quantum mechanics were not reported to date.

title: From Buffers to Registers: Unlocking Fine-Grained FlashAttention with Hybrid-Bonded 3D NPU Co-Design
creator: Jinxin Yu, Yudong Pan, Mengdi Wang, Huawei Li, Yinhe Han, Xiaowei Li, Ying Wang, [4pt] SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China
description: Abstract Transformer-based models dominate modern AI workloads but exacerbate memory bottlenecks due to their quadratic attention complexity and ever-growing model sizes. Existing accelerators, such as Groq and Cerebras, mitigate off-chip traffic with large on-chip caches, while algorithmic innovations such as FlashAttention fuse operators to avoid materializing large attention matrices.

title: OSIL: Learning Offline Safe Imitation Policies with Safety Inferred from Non-preferred Trajectories Conference: Proc. of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2026); May 25 – 29, 2026; Paphos, Cyprus
creator: Returaj Burnwal, Nirav Pravinbhai Bhatt, Balaraman Ravindran
description: Abstract . This work addresses the problem of offline safe imitation learning (IL), where the goal is to learn safe and reward-maximizing policies from demonstrations that do not have per-timestep safety cost or reward information. In many real-world domains, online learning in the environment can be risky, and specifying accurate safety costs can be difficult.

title: Mask-Based Window-Level Insider Threat Detection for Campaign Discovery
creator: Jericho Cain*, Hayden Beadles
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jericho Cain*, Hayden Beadles. User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) systems commonly detect insider threats by scoring fixed time windows of user activity for anomalous behavior. While this window-level paradigm has proven effective for identifying sharp behavioral deviations, it remains unclear how much information about longer-running attack campaigns is already present within individual windows, and how such information can be leveraged for campaign discovery.

title: Information Abstraction for Data Transmission Networks based on Large Language Models
creator: Haoyuan Zhu, Haonan Hu, Jie Zhang
description: Abstract Biological systems, particularly the human brain, achieve remarkable energy efficiency by abstracting information across multiple hierarchical levels. In contrast, modern artificial intelligence and communication systems often consume significant energy overheads in transmitting low-level data, with limited emphasis on abstraction. Despite its implicit importance, a formal and computational theory of information abstraction remains absent.

title: Reality Copilot: Voice-First Human–AI Collaboration in Mixed Reality Using Large Multimodal Models DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2026/06 CCS: Human-centered
creator: Liuchuan Yu, Yongqi Zhang, Lap-Fai Yu
description: Abstract . Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) have shown strong potential for assisting users in tasks, such as programming, content creation, and information access, yet their interaction remains largely limited to traditional interfaces such as desktops and smartphones. Meanwhile, advances in mixed reality (MR) hardware have enabled applications that extend beyond entertainment and into everyday use.

title: Normalized Surveillance in the Datafied Car: How Autonomous Vehicle Users Rationalize Privacy Trade-offs
creator: Yehuda Perry \affilnum 1, Tawfiq Ammari \affilnum 1
description: Abstract Autonomous vehicles (AVs) are increasingly characterized by pervasive datafication and continuous surveillance through sensor arrays including in-cabin cameras, LIDAR systems, and GPS tracking. Drawing on 16 semi-structured interviews with AV drivers analyzed using constructivist grounded theory, this study examines how users make sense of vehicular surveillance within the broader context of everyday datafication.

title: Strong potential in a box for applications to femtoscopy
creator: Gleb Romanenko, Francesca Bellini
description: Abstract Understanding the short-range nucleon–nucleon interaction is essential for the interpretation of correlation femtoscopy measurements in high-energy hadronic and nuclear collisions. We present an analytical treatment of the strong interaction in two-nucleon systems by modeling it with a square-well potential and solving the Schrödinger equation in the presence of the Coulomb interaction.

title: Population Properties of Binary Black Holes with Eccentricity
creator: M. Zeeshan, R. O’Shaughnessy, N. Malagon
description: Abstract The improved sensitivity of Gravitational-Wave detectors and the development of eccentric waveform models enable us to explore the growing catalog of gravitational-wave events with measurable eccentricity. This opens new opportunities to gain insight into the formation channels and evolutionary pathways of compact binary systems using eccentricity.

title: Endo-Twisted Conjugacy and Outer Fixed Points in Solvable Baumslag–Solitar Groups
creator: Mallika Roy
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mallika Roy. In this article, we solve the twisted conjugacy problem with respect to endomorphisms for solvable Baumslag–Solitar groups B ​ S ​ ( 1 , n ) BS(1,n) , i.e., we propose an algorithm which, given two elements u , v ∈ B ​ S ​ ( 1 , n ) u,v\in BS(1,n) and an endomorphism ψ ∈ End ⁡ ( B ​ S ​ ( 1 , n ) ) \psi\in\operatorname{End}(BS(1,n)) , decides whether v = ( x ​ ψ ) −

title: Fake stationary rough Heston volatility: Microstructure-inspired foundations Emmanuel Gnabeyeu and Mathieu Rosenbaum gratefully acknowledge support from the ILB Chair Artificial Intelligence and Quantitative Methods for Finance at University Paris Dauphine-PSL.
creator: Emmanuel Gnabeyeu, Gilles Pagès, Mathieu Rosenbaum
description: Abstract This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of suitably time-modulated Hawkes processes with heavy-tailed kernels in a nearly unstable regime. We show that, under appropriate scaling, both the intensity processes and the rescaled Hawkes processes converge to a mean-reverting, time-inhomogeneous rough fractional square-root process and its integrated counterpart, respectively.

title: Induced dynamics and quasifactors for minimal equicontinuous actions on Stone spaces Thanks: This article was funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) – 530703788.
creator: María Isabel Cortez, Till Hauser
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by María Isabel Cortez, Till Hauser. A minimal equicontinuous action of a group G G on a Stone space X X is called a subodometer . If such a subodometer arises from a group rotation, we refer to it as an odometer . For subodometers ( X , G ) (X,G) we show that the hyperspace ℋ ⁡ ( X ) {\mathcal{H}}(X) - given by all closed subsets of X X and the Vietoris topology - decomposes into subodometers.

title: Towards Term-based Verification of Diagrammatic Equivalence
creator: Julie Cailler, Noé Delorme, Simon Perdrix, Sophie Tourret
description: Abstract A string diagram is a two-dimensional graphical representation that can be described as a one-dimensional term generated from a set of primitives using sequential and parallel compositions. Since different syntactic terms may represent the same diagram, this syntax is quotiented by a collection of coherence equations expressing equivalence up to deformation.

title: Complexity of the p p -spin Hamiltonian with a Non-Rotationally Invariant Potential
creator: Wei-Kuo Chen, Te-Lun Lu, Arnab Sen
description: Abstract We investigate the complexity of the Hamiltonian in the pure p p -spin spin glass model accompanied with a polynomial-type potential on ℝ N \mathbb{R}^{N} . In this Hamiltonian, the Gaussian field is anisotropic, and the potential lacks rotational invariance.

title: Bayesian inference for tidal heating with extreme mass ratio inspirals
creator: Zhong-Wu Xia 1 , Sheng Long 2 , Qiyuan Pan 1,3 , Jiliang Jing 1,3 and Wei-Liang Qian 4,5,3
description: Abstract Abstract Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) provide unique probes of near-horizon dissipation through the tidal heating. We present a full Bayesian analysis of tidal heating in equatorial eccentric EMRIs by performing injection–recovery studies and inferring posterior constraints on the reflectivity parameter | ℛ | 2 |\mathcal{R}|^{2} while sampling in the full EMRI parameter space.

title: Exploiting the Structure in Tensor Decompositions for Matrix Multiplication Conference: ; ; Thanks: ∗ M. Kauers was supported by the Austrian FWF grants 10.55776/PAT8258123, 10.55776/I6130, and 10.55776/PAT9952223 Thanks: † J. Moosbauer was supported by the Austrian FWF grant 10.55776/PAT8258123 Tha
creator: Manuel Kauers ∗, Jakob Moosbauer †, Isaac Wood ‡
description: Abstract . We present a new algorithm for fast matrix multiplication using tensor decompositions which have special features. Thanks to these features we obtain exponents lower than what the rank of the tensor decomposition suggests. In particular for 6 × 6 6\times 6 matrix multiplication we reduce the exponent of the recent algorithm by Moosbauer and Poole from 2.8075 2.

title: How fast does the range of simple random walk grow?
creator: Itai Benjamini, Justin Salez
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Itai Benjamini, Justin Salez. Consider a discrete-time simple random walk ( X t ) t ≥ 0 (X_{t})_{t\geq 0} on an infinite, connected, locally finite graph G G . Let R t := | { X 0 , … , X t } | R_{t}:=|\{X_{0},\dots,X_{t}\}| denote its range at time t t , and T n := inf { t ≥ 0 : R t = n } T_{n}:=\inf\{t\geq 0:R_{t}=n\} the n − n- th discovery time.

title: A Dynamical Microscope for Multivariate Oscillatory Signals: Validating Regime Recovery on Shared Manifolds Journal: NeuroImage
creator: Łukasz Furman, Ludovico Minati, Włodzisław Duch
description: Abstract Multivariate oscillatory signals from complex systems often exhibit non-stationary dynamics and metastable regime structure, making dynamical interpretation challenging. We introduce a “dynamical microscope” framework that converts multichannel signals into circular phase–amplitude features, learns a data-driven latent trajectory representation with an autoencoder, and quantifies dynamical regimes through trajectory geometry and flow field metrics.

title: A statistic-swapping involution on the Cartesian product of the symmetric group S k ​ n S_{kn} and the generalized symmetric group S ⁡ ( k , n ) S(k,n)
creator: Peter Kagey, Kai Mawhinney
description: Abstract We construct a statistic-swapping involution on the Cartesian product of the generalized symmetric group S ⁡ ( k , n ) S(k,n) with the symmetric group S k ​ n S_{kn} , which swaps the number of fixed points in the generalized symmetric group element with the number of k k -cycles in the symmetric group element.

title: MoToRec: Sparse-Regularized Multimodal Tokenization for Cold-Start Recommendation
creator: Jialin Liu, Zhaorui Zhang, Ray C.C. Cheung
description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) have revolutionized recommender systems by effectively modeling complex user-item interactions, yet data sparsity and the item cold-start problem significantly impair performance, particularly for new items with limited or no interaction history. While multimodal content offers a promising solution, existing methods result in suboptimal representations for new items due to noise and entanglement in sparse data.

title: Motion Capture is Not the Target Domain: Scaling Synthetic Data for Learning Motion Representations
creator: Firas Darwish, George Nicholson, Aiden Doherty, Hang Yuan
description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Firas Darwish, George Nicholson, Aiden Doherty, Hang Yuan. Synthetic data offers a compelling path to scalable pretraining when real-world data is scarce, but models pretrained on synthetic data often fail to transfer reliably to deployment settings. We study this problem in full-body human motion, where large-scale data collection is infeasible but essential for wearable-based Human Activity Recognition (HAR), and where synthetic motion can be generated from motion-capture–derived representations.
